task_description: Write a method in Dafny to find the length of the smallest list in a list of lists.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method LengthOfSmallestList(lists: seq<seq<int>>) returns (minLength: nat)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The returned value is the length of the shortest list in the input sequence of lists
    - For every list in the input, its length is greater than or equal to the returned value
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method SmallestListLength(lists: seq<seq<int>>) returns (length: int)

Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The input list of lists should not be empty; i.e., there should be at least one list
Dafny specification:
    requires |lists| > 0

Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The returned length should be equal to the length of the shortest list in the input
- The length should be at least 0 (since list lengths are non-negative)

Dafny specification:
    ensures length >= 0
    ensures exists i :: 0 <= i < |lists| && length == |lists[i]|
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |lists| ==> length <= |lists[i]|

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
method SmallestListLength(lists: seq<seq<int>>) returns (length: int)
    requires |lists| > 0
    ensures length >= 0
    ensures exists i :: 0 <= i < |lists| && length == |lists[i]|
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |lists| ==> length <= |lists[i]|
{
    length := |lists[0]|;
    var i := 1;
    while i < |lists|
        invariant 1 <= i <= |lists|
        invariant length >= 0
        invariant exists j :: 0 <= j < i && length == |lists[j]|
        invariant forall j :: 0 <= j < i ==> length <= |lists[j]|
    {
        if |lists[i]| < length {
            length := |lists[i|;
        }
        i := i + 1;
    }
}
```
